events.what: Vega claims an elementary proof that no quasiperfect number exists (preprints.org)
events.credibility_reason: F5: about 15 months with no evaluations or expert uptake on a classical problem where a resolution would be a landmark; the author has a record of unaccepted claims on P vs NP and Riemann-hypothesis variants; the venue is not peer-reviewed; a short elementary 'note' uses a method this divisor-sum problem is known to resist; and the Alekseyev (2026) and Toyohara–Tao–Yao (2026) papers still treat existence as open. The record also admits the preprint text was never opened (403s).

events.what: Alekseyev raises the lower bound on a quasiperfect number from 10^35 to 10^45
Toyohara, Tao and Yao show every quasiperfect number has at least eight distinct prime factors
AI-agent-built GitHub repository claiming an unfinished omega(N)>=15 bound
events.credibility_reason: Unfinished: its own abstract contains an unresolved template placeholder '10^{TelemetryMaxLog}'; no paper and no uptake.
events.ai_basis: Record: developed almost entirely through AI-agent-authored pull requests ('google-labs-stitch[bot]', 'Jitro').

judgement.doubts: The status could rest on either 2026 bound; both are human and non-AI, so the codes do not change. The researcher never read the full text of either paper, so an AI disclosure in the acknowledgements cannot be ruled out. Pith is an automated review and verifies nothing (F11). The Lean part is partial and adds no verification (F10).

corrections.why: F5/F8: credited_humans should list the authors of the events the status rests on, the two 2026 bounds. Vega's claim is set aside as not credible: the record's own summary says it has no evaluations and comes from an author whose earlier claims on famous problems were not accepted, and later papers still treat the problem as open. It stays in disputes as evidence.

other: kept. The record's summary calls the eight-prime-factor result 'partial-grade progress on a case', but a larger minimum count of prime factors is a bound on a question that stays open (F3), so progress is the right code. The one whole-scope claim (Vega) is discarded under F5.
